jessica (Support): Hey team quick escalation from a paid customer — they say users who previously checked 'remember this device' are being forced to re‑MFA after a maintenance window. Happening across web and mobile, started ~10:05 UTC after we rolled a small auth change. Customer reports session cookie still present but MFA prompt appears.

ayan (SRE): Thanks — any error IDs or example session cookies they sent over?

jessica (Support): Pasted what they provided. They redacted PII but left cookie names and a short session token: `session=eyJhbGci...` They also sent a screenshot of the MFA dialog and note the device trust toggle had been checked. They saw 401s during some background calls around the same time.

mike (Eng): Which release rolled at 10:00? I pulled the deploys — there was a tiny auth flag flip to change how 'remember_device' is stored (migrating from cookie->db flag). deploy-bot: release/2026-03-15/auth-device-flag-migrate deployed at 10:03 UTC to prod. :rocket:

deploy-bot: automated rollback not triggered.

lena (Security): Uh — that migration touches the device trust surface. Did we run a compatibility shim? We should have honored both cookie and DB flag during migration window.

mike (Eng): We intended to keep a read-path for both, but there's a TTL on the legacy cookie->db mapping job. Possible mismatch where older cookies were no longer being interpreted as trusted if the mapping job failed. Can we get an audit on the mapping job and auth logs for that customer's org?

ayan (SRE): On it. Checking job controller logs and auth service traces now. Running query for mapping job failures between 09:50-10:10 UTC.

ayan (SRE): Found intermittent 502 from mapping-worker at 10:01-10:04. Evidence: snippet of worker logs: ```
[10:01:17 UTC] ERROR mapping-worker - POST /map-cookie 502 upstream timeout
[10:02:01 UTC] ERROR mapping-worker - POST /map-cookie 502 upstream timeout
[10:03:05 UTC] INFO mapping-worker - fallback to legacy-cookie-parse
```

mike (Eng): That 'fallback to legacy-cookie-parse' should keep behavior stable but only if the auth service actually consults legacy parse when DB mapping fails. Do we have auth service logs indicating it consulted legacy flow?

ayan (SRE): Looking... auth-service logs for that org show: ```
[10:02:59] WARN auth - device-trust-eval: mapping-missed, attempting legacy-parse
[10:03:01] ERROR auth - legacy-parse failed: cookie-decoder-v2 threw UnexpectedPaddingError
[10:03:02] INFO auth - auth-result: require_mfa=true (reason=legacy-parse-failed)
```

jessica (Support): Customer says their cookie was issued months ago, would it be using older encoding?

mike (Eng): Yes. We rolled cookie-decoder-v2 last quarter; it should decode older tokens but there are edge cases when the cookie was double-encoded by some proxies (we saw a small subset historically). If decoder throws, we mark as unknown and force MFA to be safe. That's what's triggering re‑prompts.

lena (Security): For compliance we definitely need the fail‑safe to force MFA. But we should limit blast radius and notify affected sessions instead of blanket reauth for entire org. Can we short-circuit for devices that have valid recent activity and idempotent signals?

mike (Eng): Short‑term mitigation: we can accept legacy cookie format again by reverting a strict validation check. That would restore remembered devices for affected users. I'll prepare a hotfix and a config flag to re-enable permissive decoding for a bounded window. Long term we need a robust migration and a verification sweep.

ayan (SRE): Agreed. Also will re-run mapping-worker with backfilled queue for the failed timeframe to rehydrate DB flags where possible. That should fix users whose cookies can be mapped.

jessica (Support): Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate after we patch. They want command line curl to check whether their session will still require MFA. Suggested snippet: ```
curl -i -H "Cookie: session=REDACTED; remember_device=1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/check-device
``` They also want to know if clearing cookies will help — we advised that'll force fresh login but isn't ideal.

mike (Eng): Hotfix plan: revert strict decoder in auth service (config toggle) -> deploy to canary (10:40) -> monitor 10m -> roll to prod 10:55. Will include feature flag so we can re-enable strict decoding after a migration verification window.

deploy-bot: starting canary deploy release/2026-03-15/auth-device-decode-hotfix to prod-canary at 10:40 UTC

ayan (SRE): I'll watch auth errors and 401 rate. If legacy-parse failure rate drops back to baseline we'll proceed. Also scheduling the mapping-worker backfill to run at 11:00 UTC (low traffic window).

lena (Security): Mike add a soft notice in the console UI for affected orgs if possible — "We detected an authentication compatibility issue; please re-authenticate or contact support" — to be safer for users.

mike (Eng): Can do. I'll add a temporary banner for the org IDs affected by mapping-worker failures.

jessica (Support): Customer just replied — appreciates quick action and asked whether we rotate session tokens as part of the fix. They want explicit confirmation that no session hijack risk introduced.

lena (Security): Confirm: we are not relaxing signature checks, just the strict padding/encoding validation on legacy decoder. No token signature verification bypass. I'll sign off on the hotfix once code diff reviewed.

mike (Eng): Pushed PR, @lena please review. Diff includes toggle and unit tests for fallback decode.

lena (Security): Reviewing now. Looks fine. Approve.

deploy-bot: canary deploy successful at 10:42 UTC.

ayan (SRE): Observability: legacy-parse-failed warnings dropped from 12% -> 0.8% during canary for sampled orgs. 401s correlated with device-trust checks dropped similarly. Backfill scheduled and started at 11:00.

mike (Eng): Rolling to prod 10:55. deploy-bot: prod roll started.

deploy-bot: prod roll complete at 10:57 UTC.

jessica (Support): Customer reports partial recovery for a subset of users — some still seeing MFA prompt. I told them we are backfilling DB flags and suggested they ask affected users to reauthenticate for immediate resolution.

ayan (SRE): Backfill results: 83% of target cookies rehydrated to DB flags. The remaining 17% had malformed cookies that cannot be mapped; those will require reauth. We will provide a CSV of affected user IDs for support to notify.

jessica (Support): Great — please drop the CSV in the secure share. I'll coordinate customer comms and mark the ticket P1 until they're fully validated.

lena (Security): We'll also open a follow-up to add an automated pre-check during migrations and add monitoring alert for mapping-worker error spikes.

mike (Eng): Long term: reissue device tokens with clear versioning and deprecate legacy encodings; run a migration that forces reissue at safe cadence and not during maintenance windows.

jessica (Support): Thanks all — I'll update the customer and close the loop after they confirm. :thumbsup:

ayan (SRE): Adding postmortem tag to this thread for follow-up.

jessica (Support): Filing ticket now: INC-2026-831 (MFA: remembered device drop after auth flag migration).
